name: setup_dev_venv
description: Local/dev-testing only -- never relevant to a real production install. Creates a .venv inside this plugin's own directory and installs requirements.txt into it, isolating its Python dependencies from every other plugin sharing this same development machine/user. Production never needs this: each plugin there gets its own dedicated OS user instead, which already isolates it without a venv. Once created, both main.py and install.sh pick .venv up automatically on every subsequent run/install, with no further configuration. install_generated_plugin now calls this itself, automatically, for the same location, before it touches the real hub -- you don't need to call this separately just to prepare for an install any more. Still call this directly BEFORE running the plugin's own tests/ via run_shell_command, since those import plugin.py and need the same dependencies importable and install_generated_plugin isn't part of that path. Also call this directly with force afterwards if requirements.txt changes, to rebuild rather than reuse a now-stale .venv. Idempotent either way: if a working .venv already exists, this is a cheap no-op -- safe to call (or have called automatically) before every test run or install attempt without re-downloading/reinstalling anything. Pass force only when requirements.txt changed or the venv is suspected broken, to rebuild it from scratch.

location.description: The subdirectory name under the server's plugin output root -- the same 'location' generate_plugin_scaffold/install_generated_plugin use.

force.description: Rebuild the .venv from scratch even if one already exists -- use after editing requirements.txt, or if the existing .venv is suspected broken. Defaults to false (reuse an existing, working .venv as-is).
